summary: We're building ExploreNation, a network of local city magazines in the US and abroad. Each edition tells positive, true stories about the people and places in its area, with a guide to the local businesses that serve it, so locals can find them.
audience: Local businesses that serve their own area and want the people there to find them. Think of a family law office, a child care center, a summer camp or a pediatrician. Cause and volunteer groups are welcome too, and can be featured in the SERVE section.
problem:
Before: locals looking for places to go and people to support don't know the business is there, and the business has no easy way to show up where people read about their own city.
After: the business is listed by what it does, its card sits right inside the stories locals are reading, and no competitor in its trade shares that spot.
moments:
They hear an edition is coming to their area and want to be in it from launch day.
They want locals to find them by what they do, not only by name.
They see the partner spot for their trade is still open and want it before a competitor takes it.
They want readers to get to know the people behind the business.
They run a cause or volunteer group and want it seen.
offerings:
Free ExploreNation listing, so locals can find you by what you do and how to reach you. Paid upgrades available.
Partner spot: six per section, one per trade, shown on every story in that section. Your partner card is made from your listing, so there's nothing to design.
Content studio in your dashboard for making your own short videos, pictures and flyers (comes with the partner spot and the bigger monthly packages)
Sponsored feature: a story about your business written by our staff, always labeled as sponsored
Printed magazine (planned): six times a year, with full-page Partner Profiles and cover ads, sold on its own
howItRuns:
It's online, on phones and computers. Each area has its own edition with five sections, LIVE, WORK, EXPLORE, SERVE and BUILD, each split into topics like neighborhoods, things to do and small business. Partner cards rotate around each story in a section. ExploreNation isn't live yet. Editions open in turn, and the free call tells you when your area's edition is planned to open. We also run weekly intro sessions.
The free call is 15 minutes with the NowTRANSFORMED team, who go over the options and rates. After the call, you choose a listing, a partner spot or a feature, and you're there from launch day.
faqs:
Q: How much does it cost?
A: A basic listing is free. Partner spots and sponsored features have regular rates, and you get the exact numbers on the free call. If you're a good fit, you may qualify for a NowTRANSFORMED sponsorship toward this offer. For ExploreNation, that's a code for our lower founding rate.

Q: Is ExploreNation live yet?
A: Not yet. Editions are being built in the US and abroad, and they open in turn. On the free call we'll tell you when your area's edition is planned to open.

Q: Do I need to design an ad?
A: No. Your partner card is made from your listing.

Q: Is the coverage only positive?
A: We focus on positive, true stories about local people and places. Anything paid is always clearly labeled, so readers can trust the rest.

Q: Will there be a printed magazine?
A: One is planned, six times a year, with full-page Partner Profiles and cover ads. It's sold on its own, not with a partner spot, and the founding-rate code doesn't cover it.
aboutYou:
We're ExploreNation, a network of local city magazines being built in the US and abroad. Many of our regular stories are reported by local young people, NowTRANSFORMED Ambassadors, who are learning to interview, write and take photos with coaching. Their name goes on their work, so every story helps them build a real portfolio.

Sponsored features are different. Our staff writes them, and they're always labeled.

Locals want to know what's good near them. We want them to find it in their own area's edition, and to find the businesses that serve them right next to those stories.
mustNotSay:
No prices on the page.
Never name a city or edition, and never promise a launch date. When an area opens is for the free call.
Never present paid content as news. Sponsored features are always labeled as sponsored.
Don't promise readers, traffic or new customers.
